# TALED historical background

## Editing-window problem

Mitochondrial A-to-G base editing can produce intended and bystander products within an accessible substrate window. Narrowing that distribution while preserving useful target activity requires a mechanism that changes relative access, timing, or substrate presentation rather than simply lowering all activity.

## Lessons from the archived case

Mechanistic language is not enough. A geometry or kinetic proposal must define a differentiating prediction, measure target-only and multi-edit molecules, and show that an apparent purity gain is not caused by total activity collapse or mitochondrial damage.

## Publication boundary

This synthetic historical bundle describes learning points only. It is not the original TALED run and does not expose its private prompts, provider output, or user evaluations.
